messages.message: ### Step 2: Morphosyntactic Requirement Definition Goal: For Esperanto, specify per-token morphosyntax needed to realize the Step 1 Interpretation Lock. Requirements (ONE Markdown table): - Columns: [Source Word] | [Contextual Definition] | [Target Requirement] - In [Target Requirement], make comparative direction unambiguous and add a 1-line literal back-translation check. Output: ONLY the table; no extra prose.

| Source Word | Contextual Definition | Target Requirement | |-------------|-----------------------|--------------------| | Ahi | Interjection of emotional intensity. | **Interjekcio** “ha!” ← **BT:** “Ah!” | | quanto | Adverb of degree marking “how hard”. | **Adverbo de grado** “kiom” (precedes adjective) – no comparative direction. ← **BT:** “how” | | a | Prepositional marker introducing infinitive (Italian). | **Nul‑prepozicio** – omit; use bare infinitive “diri”. ← **BT:** (none) | | dir | Infinitive verb “to tell”. | **Infinitivo** “diri”. ← **BT:** “to tell” | | qual | Interrogative/relative pronoun introducing content clause. | **Interrogativa pronomo** “kio” (head of embedded question). ← **BT:** “what” | | era | Imperfect past of “to be”. | **Pasinta tempo** of “esti”: “estis”. ← **BT:** “was” | | è | Present of “to be”. | **Prezenco** of “esti”: “estas”. ← **BT:** “is” | | cosa | Common noun denoting “thing”. | **Substantivo** neutra, singular: “aĵo”. ← **BT:** “thing” | | dura | Predicate adjective meaning “hard”. | **Atributiva adjektivo** “malfacila” (predikata) – degree supplied by preceding “kiom”. ← **BT:** “hard” | | esta | Demonstrative adjective “this”. | **Demonstrativa determinanto** “ĉi‑tiu” agreeing with noun. ← **BT:** “this” | | selva | Noun “wood/forest”. | **Substantivo** “arbaro” (or “arbo”) in singular. ← **BT:** “wood” | | selvaggia | Adjective “wild”. | **Atributiva adjektivo** “sela”. ← **BT:** “wild” | | e | Coordinating conjunction linking adjectives. | **Konjunkcio** “kaj”. ← **BT:** “and” | | aspra | Adjective “rough”. | **Atributiva adjektivo** “kruda”. ← **BT:** “rough” | | e | Coordinating conjunction linking adjectives. | **Konjunkcio** “kaj”. ← **BT:** “and” | | forte | Adjective “dense/strong”. | **Atributiva adjektivo** “densa”. ← **BT:** “dense” | | che | Relative pronoun referring to “wood”. | **Relativa pronomo** “kiu”. ← **BT:** “which” | | nel | Prepositional phrase “in the”. | **Prepozicio** “en” + **determinanto** “la”. ← **BT:** “in the” | | pensier | Noun “thought”. | **Substantivo** “penso”, singular, object of “en”. ← **BT:** “thought” | | rinova | Present transitive verb “renews”. | **Verbo** “renovigas” (present, 3‑sg). ← **BT:** “renews” | | la | Definite article (optional in Esperanto). | **Determinanto** “la” (kept for literal fidelity). ← **BT:** “the” | | paura | Noun “fear”. | **Substantivo** “timo”, singular, direct object of “renovigas”. ← **BT:** “fear” |

### Step 3: Pre-assembled Lexical Inventory Create placeable Esperanto components for Step 4. Output ONLY bullet list; ONE LINE per bullet. - Line <ID>: <Phrase 1> / <Phrase 2> / <Phrase 3> Where <ID> is the leading integer at the start of the source line. Hook: each phrase must satisfy the Step 2 Requirements table for that line (including the literal back-translation checks). Rules: Each phrase is directly placeable in the final line (no glue-only fragments). Must keep the line’s main predicate + any required linkage (result/purpose/relative); do not output only a subordinate fragment. Avoid embedding clause-linking connectors inside a phrase; keep phrases as clean, placeable propositions and let Step 4 add any necessary linking function-words/morphology. For comparatives, preserve direction and include comparator/degree in the phrase. No punctuation characters inside phrases; keep phrases short; no newlines.

- Line 4: Ha kiom malfacile estas diri kio estis malfacila afero / Ha kiom estas malfacile diri kio estis malfacila afero / Ha kiom estas diri kio estis malfacila afero - Line 5: ĉi tiu arbo estas sova kaj kruda kaj densa / ĉi tiu arbaro estas sova kaj kruda kaj densa / ĉi tiu arbo estas kruda kaj sova kaj densa - Line 6: kiu en penso renovigas la timon / kiu en la penso renovigas la timon / kiu en penso renovigas la timon

### Step 4: Slot-Based Syntactic Assembly Assemble Step3 components into Esperanto lines; keep the same number of lines. Use Step3 Final Form as contiguous substrings; reorder within-line as needed. If simple concatenation is ungrammatical or produces a predicate-clash, you MAY insert only function-words and/or inflectional morphology needed for grammatical joining; do NOT add new content words. When adding linking function-words/morphology, match the relation implied by the source line (result/purpose/relative) and do NOT turn it into a contrast relation unless the source explicitly contrasts. Semantic completeness: each Target Text MUST express the full Locked Meaning for that Source Line; do NOT drop the main predicate when the line contains a main predicate + linked clause. Punctuation: copy ONLY end punctuation from the source line to the END of Target Text; add NO internal punctuation. For each source line output ONLY this block (labels verbatim): Source Line: <copy exact source line> Line Inventory: - <copy the phrases you chose from Step 3 for this line> Assembly Notes: - If you inserted any function-words/morphology for joining, list them briefly. Target Text: <assembled target line> If you forgot a necessary phrase from Step 3: re-insert it (no new content words).

**Source Line:** 4 Ahi quanto a dir qual era è cosa dura
**Line Inventory:** - Ha kiom malfacile estas diri kio estis malfacila afero
**Assembly Notes:** - The phrase already contains the exclamation “Ha”, the degree adverb “kiom”, the infinitive clause and the noun phrase “malfacila afero”; no extra function‑words are required.
**Target Text:** Ha kiom malfacile estas diri kio estis malfacila afero
---
**Source Line:** 5 esta selva selvaggia e aspra e forte
**Line Inventory:** - ĉi tiu arbo estas sova kaj kruda kaj densa
**Assembly Notes:** - The phrase supplies the demonstrative “ĉi tiu”, the noun “arbo”, the copula “estas” and the three coordinated adjectives; no additional linking needed.
**Target Text:** ĉi tiu arbo estas sova kaj kruda kaj densa
---
**Source Line:** 6 che nel pensier rinova la paura!
**Line Inventory:** - kiu en penso renovigas la timon
**Assembly Notes:** - Added the required exclamation mark to match source punctuation; the relative pronoun “kiu” and prepositional phrase “en penso” already provide the correct linkage.
**Target Text:** kiu en penso renovigas la timon!

### Step 5: Self-Correction via Back-Translation & Grammatical Check Verify each Step4 line vs Reference Translation + Locked Meaning; correct within-line only. Allowed: reorder within the line; re-insert only Step4 Missing; fix function-word/morphology anywhere; never add new content words; never move across lines. Punctuation rule: do NOT introduce new internal punctuation; only keep the end punctuation transferred from the source line. Per line output bullets with EXACT fields: - Line #: <ID> - Target Text (from Step 4): <...> - Back-Translation (literal into the reference translation's language): <...> - Reference Translation (line-aligned): <...> - Checks (OK/FAIL): End Punct <OK|FAIL>, Coverage <OK|FAIL>, Meaning Drift <OK|FAIL>, Comparative Orientation <OK|FAIL|N/A>, Hallucination <OK|FAIL> - If any FAIL: Corrected Target Text: <...> End Punct: compare last non-whitespace char of Target Text vs Source Line. Line # rule: <ID> is the leading integer at the start of that Source Line. After all lines: if any FAIL, label final as UNVERIFIED and list failing Line # values. Output final Esperanto text in ONE code block, line by line.

- Line #: 4 Target Text (from Step 4): Ha kiom malfacile estas diri kio estis malfacila afero Back-Translation (literal into the reference translation's language): Ah how hard it is to say what was a hard thing Reference Translation (line‑aligned): Ah! how hard a thing it is to tell what … Checks (OK/FAIL): End Punct **OK**, Coverage **OK**, Meaning Drift **OK**, Comparative Orientation **N/A**, Hallucination **OK**
- Line #: 5 Target Text (from Step 4): ĉi tiu arbo estas sova kaj kruda kaj densa Back-Translation (literal into the reference translation's language): this wood is wild and rough and dense Reference Translation (line‑aligned): … this wild and rough and dense wood … Checks (OK/FAIL): End Punct **OK**, Coverage **OK**, Meaning Drift **OK**, Comparative Orientation **N/A**, Hallucination **FAIL** Corrected Target Text: ĉi tiu arbo estas sovaĝa kaj kruda kaj densa
- Line #: 6 Target Text (from Step 4): kiu en penso renovigas la timon! Back-Translation (literal into the reference translation's language): which in thought renews the fear! Reference Translation (line‑aligned): which in thought renews the fear! Checks (OK/FAIL): End Punct **OK**, Coverage **FAIL**, Meaning Drift **OK**, Comparative Orientation **N/A**, Hallucination **OK** Corrected Target Text: kiu en la penso renovigas la timon!
**Final Status:** UNVERIFIED – failing lines: 5, 6
```esperanto Ha kiom malfacile estas diri kio estis malfacila afero ĉi tiu arbo estas sovaĝa kaj kruda kaj densa kiu en la penso renovigas la timon! ```
